How to enable DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) in Firefox so your ISP cannot keep track of the sites you visit.

Just because the DNS request is hidden in HTTPS doesn't mean the ISP can't see where you're going. All this does is keep the ISP from blocking certain domains from being looked up (resolved). They could still block web access to those same domains if they wanted.

Once you actually connect to the site they know exactly which site it is even if they don't know exactly what you're doing on the site.

This is no replacement for a VPN or TOR, I'm not sure what problem it fixes exactly.

The only real benefit I see is the possibility for stopping a man-in-the-middle DNS attack. The problem with this though is that you are getting DNS from some app vendor which may be more shady than your ISP. If the app vendor can install SSL certificates on your machine, and control DNS, you are just giving them man-in-the middle access.

If I'm missing something let me know but it looks like half a security idea that will expose people to more risk than going with a complete tunneling solution. It might even be an intentional exploit from the looks of it.
